This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
We say that $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ is an essential component if $d_s(A+B)>d_s(B)$ for every $B\subset \mathbb{N}$ with $0<d_s(B)<1$ where $d_s$ is the Schnirelmann density.
Is $B=\{2^m3^n : m,n\geq 0\}$ an essential component?
#1146: [Va99,1.19]
number theory
In [Ru99] Ruzsa states "The simplest set with a chance to be an essential component is the collection of numbers in the form $2^m3^n$ and Erdős often asked whether it is an essential component or not; I do not even have a plausible guess."
See also [37].

 Small convention question: under the literal positive-integer definition\[
\sigma(A)=\inf_{n\geq 1}\frac{|A\cap[1,n]|}{n},
\]the set\[
B=\{2^m3^n:m,n\geq 0\}
\]as written does not contain \(0\). Then for any set \(C\) with
\(\sigma(C)>0\), we must have \(1\in C\). Since the least element of
\(B\) is \(1\), the sumset \(B+C\) misses \(1\), and hence\[
\sigma(B+C)=0.
\]So I assume the intended question is the normalized/nontrivial one, for
example whether \(B\cup\{0\}\) is an essential component. Is that the
intended convention?
 Zeraoulia Rafik

 I believe so, yes; when dealing with the Schnirelmann density of sumsets, the appropriate sumset (sometimes denoted with $A \oplus B$) is generally defined as $$\{a+b : a \in A \cup \{0\}, b \in B \cup \{0\}\}.$$
